title: Exceptional-Point-Anchored Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Non-Hermitian Many-Body Phase Diagrams: Bridging Skin-Effect Topology and Entanglement Criticality on NISQ Hardware
authors: Akoramurthy B, Surendiran B, Xiaochun Cheng
abstract: We introduce the Biorthogonal Variational Quantum Eigensolver (B-VQE), a quantum algorithm for simulating non-Hermitian many-body systems on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. Non-Hermitian quantum matter exhibits exceptional points, parity-time symmetry breaking, and non-Hermitian skin effects, yet existing quantum algorithms often rely on costly post-selection procedures and are not designed to capture biorthogonal eigenstates.   B-VQE employs independent variational circuits to represent the left and right eigenstates of a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and optimizes a biorthogonal objective function that directly tracks non-Hermitian phase transitions. The framework incorporates an Exceptional-Point Detector (EPD) that identifies exceptional points through a hardware-native coalescence metric and a Non-Hermitian Quantum Geometric Tensor (NH-QGT) readout that distinguishes state-topological and band-topological signatures in interacting many-body systems. To overcome the exponential overhead associated with conventional non-Hermitian simulation, we develop an importance-sampling mitigation strategy that removes the need for ancilla-based post-selection while retaining polynomial computational scaling.   We validate the approach on three representative models: a non-Hermitian Hubbard chain, a non-Hermitian XXZ spin chain, and a two-dimensional non-Hermitian (t)-(J) model. B-VQE achieves relative energy errors below (5\times10^{-3}) and locates exceptional points with high accuracy on noise-free simulations while resolving phase boundaries associated with localization, quantum scars, and skin-effect physics. These results establish B-VQE as a scalable NISQ methodology for constructing non-Hermitian many-body phase diagrams and exploring topological and critical phenomena in open quantum systems.
summary: The paper introduces the Biorthogonal Variational Quantum Eigensolver (B-VQE) to simulate non-Hermitian many-body physics on NISQ hardware. It overcomes limitations of previous methods by using dual circuits and importance sampling, allowing for accurate mapping of phase diagrams that exhibit topological features like skin effects and exceptional points. This establishes B-VQE as a scalable tool for studying open quantum systems.
main_problem: Developing a scalable quantum algorithm to simulate non-Hermitian many-body systems on NISQ hardware, which is challenging due to the lack of standard eigenvalue formulations.
main_result: The Biorthogonal VQE (B-VQE) successfully maps out complex phase diagrams, detects exceptional points (EPs), and characterizes topological transitions with polynomial overhead scaling.
method: It employs a dual-circuit ansatz to approximate left and right eigenstates and minimizes a specialized biorthogonal cost function. Importance-sampling mitigation is used to remove the need for costly post-selection.
model_or_system: The study applies to general non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, tested on specific models like the non-Hermitian Hubbard chain, NH-XXZ spin chain, and 2D t-J model. These systems exhibit phenomena such as PT-symmetry breaking and the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect.
key_observables: Biorthogonal Energy ($E_{bio}$), Coalescence Metric ($C_\lambda$), Biorthogonal Entanglement Entropy ($S_{bio}$), Loschmidt echo ($\mathcal{L}_t^2$), and Topological Chern Number ($C_{	ext{state}}$).
important_parameters: System size (N=10 sites), non-Hermiticity parameter ($\gamma$ or $\lambda$), and noise levels simulated on NISQ hardware.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the B-VQE ansatz can efficiently approximate the required biorthogonal eigenstates, and that importance sampling mitigation maintains polynomial scaling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing transitions between ergodic, MBL, and skin-localized phases; they also show $S_{bio}$ scaling laws (volume vs. area law) and the coalescence metric identifying EPs.
paper_structure: The paper introduces B-VQE for non-Hermitian systems, details the mathematical framework using biorthogonality, presents diagnostic tools like the EPD and NH-QGT, validates the approach on multiple physical models (Hubbard, XXZ, t-J), and concludes by benchmarking its scalability against classical/other quantum methods.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the frontier of applying variational quantum algorithms to open quantum systems, providing concrete, resource-aware protocols for mapping complex phase diagrams inaccessible via standard VQE techniques.

Figure 2: B-VQE circuit architecture and optimisation convergence (Qiskit-Aer simulation). (a) Dual-circuit architecture: the right-state circuit URθ (blue) and left-state circuit ULϕ (red) are built as Qiskit 2.4.1 QuantumCircuit objects with hardware-efficient ansatz layers (Ry-Rz + CNOT ladder); the biorthogonal cost function LB-VQE and EPD coalescence metric Cλ are evaluated jointly. Noise parameters are from IBM Heron r2 calibration data (ibm kingston, ibm fez, ibm marrakesh). (b) COBYLA convergence trace for γJ = 0.75 (n = 1, d = 3): the cost LB-VQE (blue) converges below the target εE = 5 × 10−3 (red dashed) within ≈120 iterations; the shaded band shows ±15% shot-noise fluctuations.
